solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cause of death, possibly, with body found in melee

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a melee is a confused brawl, a riot
the body's soft tissue is its flesh

explanation.surface: A coroner's note: someone died in a brawl and the body was discovered amid the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' reads as a corpse, but it is the flesh that goes inside the brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet fired from a long gun is one possible way a person gets killed, hence the hedge in the clue.

clue.text: Repeated piece of music before service, loud for masses

indicators.note: coming before something means standing ahead of it in sequence

blocks.note: a riff is a short repeated musical phrase
the Royal Air Force is one of the armed services
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A church concert programme: a looping tune before the service, played loudly for the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests church but stands for the Royal Air Force; 'masses' sounds liturgical but means the common people.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff is a disparaging term for ordinary common people, the crowd or rabble, which the masses also denotes.

clue.text: Female invariably creating state of excitement

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for female
ever means always, without variation

explanation.surface: A woman who always stirs up a buzz wherever she goes.
explanation.walkthrough: F for female is a standard abbreviation; 'invariably' gives the adverb meaning always.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever is used figuratively for nervous agitation or heightened enthusiasm, as in election fever.

clue.text: European bishop, in surprise, leaving West

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for European
B is the chess notation for bishop
to astound is to surprise greatly

explanation.surface: A continental cleric, to everyone's amazement, departing the Western world.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop sits inside the verb for surprise, after a leading E; 'leaving West' reads as defection but is simply a direction of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling towards the east means heading away from the west, the opposite compass direction.

clue.text: Regular visitor somewhat put in shade

indicators.note: putting something in another thing places it inside, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a shade of colour is a hue
somewhat means a bit, slightly

explanation.surface: A frequent guest who is made to feel slightly overshadowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in shade' reads as being upstaged, but shade is a colour and the phrase for somewhat goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is someone who frequents a particular place, a regular customer or caller.

clue.text: Fieldwork lasting into maturity

blocks.note: till means up until, lasting into a time
coming of age is reaching maturity

explanation.surface: A research project in the field that drags on until the researcher grows old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fieldwork' suggests academic research outdoors, but it is literally work done on fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is ploughing and cultivating land, quite literally labour carried out in farm fields.

clue.text: Stylish young woman put on cape

definitions.note: adjective, as in a class act

indicators.note: one thing put on another is joined to it, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A fashionable girl throws a cape over her shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on cape' looks like dressing up, but cape is the headland abbreviation and the girl is attached to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Class used as an informal adjective means showing quality and style, as in a class player.

clue.text: Reportedly attack king as citizen of republic

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: in chess, to attack the king is to put it in check

explanation.surface: Word has it someone assaulted a monarch, posing as an ordinary citizen of a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: The attack is the chess one: threatening the king is check, which sounds the same as the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a national of the Czech Republic, a central European country without a monarch.

clue.text: Today, most of Turkey is upset with Romania

indicators.note: upset things are knocked out of their order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item: Turkey is currently at odds with its Balkan neighbour Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of Turkey' looks like an instruction to drop a letter, but it is the definition: the peninsula forms most of modern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia, the historic peninsula called Asia Minor, makes up the greater part of present-day Turkish territory.

clue.text: Also, in short, a mixed drink

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is held by another

blocks.note: shy can mean lacking or short of, as in a few pounds shy
and adds something, meaning also

explanation.surface: A tacked-on afterthought: and, briefly, a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' reads as 'briefly', but 'in' is the container signal and 'short' means lacking. Shandy is a British drink of beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy combines beer with lemonade or ginger beer, so it is literally a blended beverage.

clue.text: Public school game in which score is four

definitions.note: a description rather than a synonym: a score, twenty, equals four of these

blocks.note: first meaning: a handball game played in walled courts at English public schools
second meaning: a score is twenty, which is four lots of five

explanation.surface: A sports report from an English private school where the final tally is four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a match result but is the old word for twenty. A British public school is a fee-paying private school; fives is a handball game played there.
explanation.definitionFit: The game takes its name from the hand, a bunch of fives, and twenty divided into units gives four such numbers.

clue.text: Some footballer in action, one noted for footwork

indicators.note: some of something is only part of it, so the letters lie within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A footballer in play, admired for skilful dribbling.
explanation.walkthrough: The footwork is not on the pitch: the definition points to dance, and the answer runs through 'footballer in action'.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical dancer depends on precise steps and pointe work, so she is famed for what her feet do.

clue.text: Savoury dish, lightly cooked — was tempted

blocks.note: rare meat is only briefly cooked
a fish that is tempted bites, taking the bait

explanation.surface: A diner tempted by a lightly cooked savoury plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was tempted' means took the bait, as a fish does when it bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a classic British savoury snack served hot.

clue.text: Tree by a large expanse of water in a sorry state

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces stand next to one another

blocks.note: the ash is a common tree
taken as written
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A tree standing beside a great sea is looking rather sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry state' suggests physical neglect, but sorry here means regretful.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ashamed means being embarrassed and regretful about something done, the sorry frame of mind.

clue.text: Bringing down to earth about what might be not true in prognostication

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other
what something might be is a possible new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: felling a tree brings it to the ground
the words as printed

explanation.surface: Deflating someone's hopes about predictions that may turn out false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing down to earth' reads as deflating, but it is literal: felling goes around the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prognostication is foretelling the future, which is exactly what a fortune-teller claims to do.

clue.text: President or first lady left in overnight accommodation

indicators.note: to be in somewhere is to be inside it, so pieces sit within another

blocks.note: a roost is where birds settle for the night
Eve was the first woman in Genesis
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A US President or his wife staying in a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a President's wife but is the first woman of the Bible; neatly, Eleanor Roosevelt was also a First Lady, so the whole clue reads both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. were both American heads of state bearing this surname.

clue.text: Learner attached to sound of poem that’s naturally attractive

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun: a thing that attracts by nature

indicators.note: attaching one thing to another joins them end to end

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
an ode is a lyric poem; with the possessive 's
tone is the quality of a sound

explanation.surface: A student drawn to the music of a poem that has natural charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of poem' is read as ode's tone, with the possessive supplying the S. 'Naturally attractive' sounds like charm but means magnetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetite rock is magnetic without any treatment, pulling iron towards it by its own nature.

clue.text: I make city attempt form of worship

blocks.note: taken as written
to do is to make or perform
LA is Los Angeles
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone who builds a city making a go of a new religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word in the first part gives a short chunk in turn; LA, Los Angeles, is a regular crossword city.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is the veneration of images or idols, one particular kind of religious devotion.

clue.text: Socially shunned — stole off to become so?

blocks.note: the straight meaning: deliberately ignored by others
the setter's reading: a stole is a wrap worn over the upper arms, and taking it off leaves that part of you chilly

explanation.surface: Someone ostracised after sneaking away, wondering if that is why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole off' looks like crept away, but stole is the noun, a shawl, which keeps the upper body warm.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is an idiom for deliberately snubbing or ignoring them.

clue.text: Optimal policy they arranged with son

indicators.note: arranging things puts them into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family plans the best strategy together with their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Son is used whole here, not abbreviated to S, and joins the other word in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says honesty is the best policy, so the clue paraphrases that familiar saying.

clue.text: University charges, under pressure, going higher

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece under another is placed after it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for university
P is the symbol for pressure
wards are people in someone's care, their charges

explanation.surface: University tuition fees, under pressure, keep rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like fees, but it means people in one's care; that word sits under the pressure symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means towards a higher position, so it describes movement that is rising.

clue.text: Put the lid on strong drink

blocks.note: first meaning: to put an end to, as with a rumour
second meaning: whisky made in Scotland

explanation.surface: Seal the bottle of hard liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as closing a bottle, but the first phrase means to stop something, a sense the verb has in 'scotch a rumour'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to quash it, and the noun is malt or blended whisky distilled north of the border.

clue.text: Sailors bragged in front of king and queen, say, on board

indicators.note: being in front of something puts it first in the line

blocks.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

blocks.clueFragment: king and queen, say, on board
blocks.note: chess pieces are called men; the king and queen are examples on the board

explanation.surface: Seamen boasting before the royal couple, perhaps aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship but means the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of a ship's company are its crew, and those men are mariners or seamen.

clue.text: Step by step demonstration of hard stuff set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: A tutorial showing, one stage at a time, how to set up something tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step by step demonstration' reads like a tutorial but is a protest on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is a public demonstration made by walking in procession, literally one step after another.

clue.text: Prodigal son taken in by Walter transformed

definitions.note: used here as a noun, a spendthrift

indicators.note: being taken in by someone means being held within them
something transformed changes its form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A wayward son welcomed back by Walter, who is a changed man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prodigal son' looks like one phrase from the parable, but only 'Prodigal' is the definition and the son is the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal, used as a noun, is someone who squanders money recklessly, just like a good-for-nothing spendthrift.

clue.text: Bishop captured in attack that’s over the top?

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a raid is a sudden attack
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman seized in an assault: was it excessive?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a loose, figurative one: going over the top suggests a military charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means fanatical or extreme in views, an excess that informally counts as over the top.

clue.text: Nothing in the growth trend right for person who speculates

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written
an upward trend is a rise
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An investor sees no upturn in the market's direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speculates' suggests a market trader to match the growth trend, but here it means someone who forms theories.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser forms hypotheses and conjectures, which is exactly what speculating means in an intellectual sense.

clue.text: Complete round-the-world trip, or just part

blocks.note: taken as written
a bit is just a part of something

explanation.surface: Take a full world tour, or only a section of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The round-the-world trip is made by a satellite, not a backpacker.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is one full circuit around a planet, such as a spacecraft travelling once around the Earth.

clue.text: Blow hot and cold, switching? That’s a problem

indicators.note: switching two things swaps their places, so their order is turned round

blocks.note: a hit is a blow
H and C are the abbreviations for hot and cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Being changeable and indecisive is a real difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow hot and cold' is the idiom for wavering, but the clue splits it into a strike plus two tap letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a temporary snag or difficulty, as in the plan went off without a hitch.

clue.text: Novel read, set between years in recent past

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a fresh order
something between two things is flanked by them, so it sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year, and the plural gives two

explanation.surface: A book I read that was set some years back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel read' looks like a book, but novel is the anagram signal and 'set' joins the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday can mean the day before today or, more loosely, the recent past, as in yesterday's news.
